answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying rewards to costly, continuous proof that fake identities cannot cheaply duplicate. Each epoch an agent answers a fresh challenge bound to its address, then needs attestations from established non-kin peers with locked stake at risk. A sybil farm must fund many aged identities producing original answers on a steady pulse, like a sparrow returning daily rather than a comet flashing once. Kinship rules block self-attestation, so splitting one operator into shells multiplies cost without multiplying payout.
